column1: # PostgreSQL-style SQL prototype: the write corpus (fork issue #29).
# Columns, separated by one TAB: id, status, checks, statement, expected.

# id: unique, lower case, words joined by hyphens. Add a case at the end of its group; never renumber or reuse an id. An id that starts with err- is a statement the server must refuse: its expected result is the SQLSTATE and the tables after it are the ones before.

# status: ok = the engine is expected to do what the server did. pending = it does not, by a decision of fork issue #29 (the ends of an edge are never updated: 0A000 with the hint to delete and insert): the case is tried and reported, never failed; when the engine does what the server did the run fails until the flag is flipped.

# checks: SELECT statements, separated by " ; ", that read the tables the statement touched, afterwards, in the same transaction. They never read the id of a new row (the two sides number new records differently). The rows of a table are compared as a multiset.

# statement: one write, with backslash, tab, line feed and carriage return written as \\, \t, \n and \r. Every case runs in a transaction that is rolled back, so the cases are independent: PostgreSQL gets the trigger and the cascade of small-writes.sql, which make id generated and a deleted vertex take its edges, as the table view of ArcadeDB does.

# expected: written by the generator from the real server, never by hand: {"result":<answer of the statement>,"after":[<answer of each check>]}. The answer of a statement without RETURNING is one row of the column count; the answers are the outcomes of answers.tsv, a table or {"error":"SQLSTATE"}. pending-server = the generator has not run on the case yet: add a case with that value, then run the generator.
# server: PostgreSQL 18.7 (Debian 18.7-1.pgdg13+5) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit
